matchups.matchup:
Anran is a hyper-mobile flanker who relies heavily on close-range combat and stacking her Ignition passive to secure eliminations. Because her Zhuque Fans are projectile-based and she lacks vertical engagement tools outside of a specifically angled Inferno Rush, she struggles to reliably threaten a high-flying Pharah. Pharah can generally bombard her from a safe altitude, forcing her to burn cooldowns to survive.

However, Anran can be incredibly elusive on the ground. Her Dancing Blaze provides total invulnerability frames, allowing her to cleanly dodge incoming Rocket Launcher splash damage. If she equips the Short Fuse Major Perk, hitting grounded allies allows her to infinitely chain her dashes, making her extremely difficult to lead with rockets. 

Pharah must also pay close attention to Anran's ultimate status. While Pharah is generally safe from the explosive impact of Vermillion Ascent, she must be extremely careful around Vermillion Revival. If Pharah secures an elimination on Anran, she must maintain her distance from the corpse; the resulting fiery explosion and immediate 100% Ignition application can easily kill a careless Pharah flying too low.
matchups.synergy: Pharah and Anran excel in a split-pressure composition. Pharah's massive splash damage forces the enemy backline to scatter and look to the sky, creating the perfect chaotic environment for Anran to dive in and rapidly build her Ignition meter on distracted targets. Because Anran benefits from the Flanker sub-role passive (granting her heavily increased healing from environmental health packs) and has immense self-sustain through the Hungering Blaze perk, Pharah's Supports are free to focus their attention entirely on keeping Pharah airborne.

matchups.matchup:
Ashe is a highly lethal hitscan threat capable of rapidly eliminating an exposed Pharah. Her Take Aim allows her to deal high burst damage at range without sacrificing too much fire rate. Pharah must utilize cover and unpredictably feather her Hover Jets to make headshots difficult. If Ashe is utilizing the Viper's Sting Major Perk, catching two consecutive scoped shots will apply an additional 25 damage-over-time, effectively negating any passive healing and forcing Pharah to retreat immediately.

While Dynamite is typically difficult to land on a hovering Pharah, Ashe becomes significantly more dangerous if she equips the Airburst Major Perk alongside the Remote Detonator Minor Perk. This combination increases the dynamite's airborne detonation radius by 40% and allows her to manually trigger it with a button press, making it incredibly easy for her to ignite Pharah mid-air without needing to land a precise shot on the explosive.

Diving Ashe is also notoriously difficult due to her Coach Gun. If she is running the Double-Barreled perk, she can violently knock Pharah away twice in rapid succession, completely resetting the engagement distance. Furthermore, Ashe's Ultimate, B.O.B., acts as an auto-aiming turret with a massive health pool. If B.O.B. is deployed, Pharah must immediately drop out of his 40-meter sightline, as he will relentlessly shoot her out of the sky.
matchups.synergy:
Ashe and Pharah excel at overwhelming the enemy's defensive cooldowns. Ashe's Dynamite deals massive damage-over-time that bypasses shields, forcing grouped enemies to scatter directly into the splash radius of Pharah's Rocket Launcher.

When Ashe deploys B.O.B., the enemy team is forced to turn their attention toward the ground to deal with his massive health pool and suppressive fire. This creates the perfect distraction for Pharah to safely take to the skybox and unleash a devastating Barrage from above without fear of immediate hitscan retaliation.

matchups.matchup:
Bastion's massive hitbox and lack of mobility make him an incredibly easy target for Pharah's Rocket Launcher. Pharah can simply abuse hard cover and corner-peek to land direct hits without exposing herself to sustained fire. However, Pharah must respect his Configuration: Assault. While in this form, his rotary cannon outputs a devastating 360 hitscan DPS, which will shred an exposed Pharah out of the sky in under a second.

Bastion's threat level changes drastically depending on his equipped Major Perk. If he runs Self-Repair, he can actively heal 90 health per second even while in Assault configuration, meaning Pharah cannot burst him down alone without fully committing to a dive. Conversely, if he equips the Lindholm Explosives Major Perk, his Assault configuration loses its hitscan rotary cannon and instead fires slow-moving explosive shells; this effectively neuters his anti-air capabilities and allows Pharah to bombard him with impunity.

His Ultimate, Configuration: Artillery, poses zero threat to an airborne Pharah, but she should remain vigilant if he equips the Armored Artillery Minor Perk, as the instant 300 overhealth makes him virtually unkillable while channeling.
matchups.synergy:
Bastion and Pharah command an overwhelming amount of raw damage and shield-break potential. When Bastion enters Configuration: Assault, the enemy team is forced to immediately seek cover behind walls and barriers. Pharah can aggressively exploit this by firing rockets around their cover, trapping enemies in a crossfire where they must choose between taking Bastion's hitscan damage or Pharah's explosive splash.

Additionally, Bastion's Configuration: Artillery forces entrenched enemies to scatter and abandon their positioning, providing Pharah with perfectly chaotic, exposed targets for a Barrage.

matchups.matchup:
Cassidy poses an extreme threat to Pharah due to the high burst damage of his hitscan Peacekeeper. A skilled Cassidy only needs two solid shots (or a single headshot) to eliminate Pharah from the sky. However, his damage falloff begins at 25 meters. Pharah's best strategy is to exploit her lack of damage falloff by bombarding Cassidy from extreme distances (30+ meters) where his shots deal significantly reduced damage.

Never engage Cassidy in close-quarters combat unless his Flashbang is on cooldown. The "hindered" effect will instantly disable Pharah's Hover Jets, Jump Jet, and Jet Dash, causing her to plummet to the ground for an easy execution. Be particularly wary if he uses the Bang Bang Minor Perk, as the second thrown Flashbang greatly extends his area of denial. Furthermore, if he is utilizing the Silver Bullet Major Perk, his secondary fire becomes a piercing hitscan shot that inflicts severe bleeding. Because this bleed damage over time ignores armor and cannot be mitigated by range, catching a stray Silver Bullet while descending can easily be fatal.

Cassidy's Ultimate, Deadeye, is incredibly dangerous to a hovering Pharah. Because Pharah is often high above the map, she is usually the first target to enter his unobstructed line of sight. Pharah must retain either Jet Dash or Concussive Blast to rapidly reposition behind hard cover when he begins channeling. Alternatively, if Pharah is close enough and has cover, she can fire a Concussive Blast at his feet to violently displace him, potentially pushing him behind a wall and breaking his line of sight to her team.
matchups.synergy:
Cassidy and Pharah form a highly complementary damage duo. Pharah's greatest weakness is her inability to contest objectives or protect her Supports on the ground. Cassidy's exceptional close-range lethality and Flashbang make him a premier anti-flanker, ensuring that the backline remains safe while Pharah operates in the skybox.

Offensively, Pharah can use Concussive Blast to physically knock entrenched enemies out from behind enemy barriers or high ground, pushing them directly into Cassidy's line of sight for an easy Peacekeeper execution or to guarantee targets for his Deadeye.

matchups.matchup:
Echo is arguably Pharah's most dangerous aerial rival, as her mobility allows her to directly contest the skybox. Because Pharah relies on predictive splash damage, hitting an erratic, free-flying Echo with the Rocket Launcher is exceptionally difficult. Echo's Tri-Shot deals massive burst damage if she closes the distance, and her Sticky Bombs can instantly spell doom if she lands a volley on Pharah mid-flight.

Pharah must meticulously manage her health pool in this matchup. If Pharah drops below 50% health, Echo's Focusing Beam will deal multiplied damage, instantly melting Pharah out of the air. This threat is magnified by the Recon Sub-Role passive, which allows Echo to see Pharah's silhouette through walls the moment she drops below half health. 

Be extremely wary if Echo is using the Focused Rush Minor Perk, which extends Focusing Beam's range to 20 meters and grants a movement speed boost, allowing her to execute Pharah from much farther away. If combined with the High Beams Major Perk, Echo will instantly reset her Flight cooldown upon securing the elimination, allowing her to safely escape back to her team.
matchups.synergy: Echo and Pharah form the classic double-flying composition. They overwhelm enemy hitscans by forcing them to look up and track two highly maneuverable aerial targets. Echo's Focusing Beam is the perfect clean-up tool, effortlessly finishing off targets that have been heavily wounded by Pharah's Rocket Launcher splash damage. Furthermore, Echo can use her Duplicate ultimate to copy an enemy Support, providing Pharah with pocket healing while completely bypassing the team's standard role limitations.

matchups.matchup:
Emre is a highly adaptable combatant whose Synthetic Burst Rifle hitscan capabilities pose a consistent threat to Pharah. Unlike other hitscan heroes, Emre suffers zero movement speed penalty while aiming down his sights. This makes him exceptionally slippery and difficult to hit with projectile rockets while he accurately bursts Pharah from afar.

While his Siphon Blaster and Cyber Frag are primarily grounded brawling tools, Pharah must be cautious if flying low to the ground against an Emre using the Cyber Adhesion Major Perk, as a stuck grenade deals an immediate 150 burst damage. 

Emre becomes an extreme threat when he activates his Ultimate, Override Protocol. The transformation grants him unrestricted flight, allowing him to directly contest Pharah in the skybox. If he equips the Suppressive Security Minor Perk, his rapid-fire light rounds will instantly slow Pharah's airborne momentum by 30%. This crippling slow makes it effortlessly easy for him to follow up with his explosive, high-damage heavy rounds. Pharah should use Jet Dash to break line of sight and wait out his 8.8-second ultimate duration.
matchups.synergy:
Emre and Pharah can completely dominate the vertical space of a map. When Emre activates Override Protocol, the team benefits from dual airborne artillery, overwhelming any hitscan heroes who cannot simultaneously track two flying targets. 

Additionally, Emre's exceptional close-quarters sustain with his Siphon Blaster perfectly covers Pharah's greatest weakness. While Pharah applies heavy splash-damage pressure from the sky, Emre can aggressively brawl on the ground to protect the team's Supports and contest the objective.

matchups.matchup:
Freja relies on complex aerial momentum and precision tracking to deal damage. While her Updraft and Quick Dash give her great vertical evasiveness, her Take Aim ability is a massive double-edged sword in an air-to-air duel. When Freja aims down her sights in the air, she suffers an 85% momentum penalty, effectively making her a hovering, stationary target. A skilled Pharah can easily capitalize on this slowdown by firing a guaranteed direct hit Rocket Launcher projectile at her.

Do not ignore her if she remains airborne. With the Aerial Recovery Major Perk, Freja passively regenerates 30 health per second after using Updraft until she touches the ground. You must commit to finishing her off or use Concussive Blast to violently knock her downward. Furthermore, be cautious of her Bola Shot ultimate. If it directly hits Pharah, it applies a severe hindered status, locking out all of Pharah's flight abilities and dragging her down into the explosive radius.
matchups.synergy: Freja and Pharah create terrifying synergistic combinations. Freja's ultimate, Bola Shot, forcefully pulls enemies within a 5-meter radius into a tightly clustered group. If Pharah coordinates her Barrage or even standard primary fire with this pull, the enemy team will be instantly obliterated by concentrated, inescapable splash damage.

matchups.matchup:
Genji possesses excellent mobility, but he generally operates at a severe disadvantage against Pharah. His Shuriken are slow-moving projectiles that are difficult to land consistently on an unpredictably hovering target, and his Swift Strike cannot gain enough altitude to reliably threaten Pharah at her maximum height.

Pharah's primary concern in this matchup is Deflect. A deflected Rocket Launcher direct hit will deal massive damage to Pharah or her airborne Support. If Genji equips the Meditation Major Perk, he will regenerate 35 health per second while deflecting; Pharah should cease firing immediately and use Concussive Blast to physically push him away from his intended dive target. 

During his Dragonblade ultimate, Pharah is entirely out of his reach. She can effortlessly use Jump Jet to gain altitude and relentlessly bombard his position, turning his ultimate into a massive liability.
matchups.synergy:
Pharah and Genji form an aggressive, multi-angled dive composition. Pharah's massive splash damage routinely softens up the enemy team, providing Genji with easy, weakened targets to secure eliminations and trigger his Swift Strike cooldown resets.

This synergy is significantly amplified if Genji equips the Blade Twisting Major Perk. Because this perk applies a 25-damage bleed effect to any enemy hit by Swift Strike who falls below half health, Pharah's rockets provide the perfect setup to instantly push targets past that critical threshold, guaranteeing Genji's executions.

matchups.matchup:
Hanzo is a lethal sniper who poses a significant threat to Pharah, but unlike hitscan heroes, his Storm Bow fires projectiles that require travel time. A Pharah utilizing unpredictable vertical thrusts and horizontal Jet Dash maneuvers will make it incredibly difficult for Hanzo to land a fatal headshot. However, if he lands a critical hit on any target, his Sharpshooter Sub-Role passive will instantly reduce the cooldown of his Lunge, making him surprisingly elusive if Pharah attempts to dive him.

Pharah must be extremely cautious of his Storm Arrows, which can quickly burst her out of the sky without requiring precise charge timing. If Hanzo is running the Scatter Arrows Major Perk, avoid diving him near enclosed spaces or high walls, as the ricocheting arrows will split and multiply, creating a wall of unavoidable burst damage.

His most dangerous tool against Pharah, however, is the Frost Arrow Major Perk. If Hanzo triggers this explosive arrow, the resulting 35% slow will drastically cripple Pharah's Hover Jets and aerial momentum for 3 seconds, effectively turning her into a sitting duck for his follow-up shots. Always maintain distance and use Concussive Blast to disrupt his aim if you suspect he has a Frost Arrow readied.
matchups.synergy:
Hanzo and Pharah excel at flushing enemies out of entrenched positions. Hanzo's Sonic Arrow provides invaluable intelligence, allowing Pharah to pre-fire her slow-moving Rocket Launcher projectiles around corners for guaranteed direct hits.

Furthermore, Hanzo's Dragonstrike forces the enemy team to immediately scatter and abandon their physical cover. Pharah can easily capitalize on this panic by hovering above the chaos and bombarding the fleeing, exposed targets with splash damage.

matchups.matchup:
Pharah is the ultimate hard counter to Junkrat. Because his Frag Launcher, Concussion Mine, and Steel Trap are entirely balanced around grounded, predictable arcs, he is practically helpless against a hovering Pharah. She can maintain maximum altitude and rain rockets down on his position without ever entering his effective threat range. Even his Ultimate, RIP-Tire, is entirely grounded, meaning Pharah can effortlessly float above it or destroy it from safety.

The only time Junkrat poses a marginal threat is if he equips the Frag Cannon Major Perk, which increases his projectile speed by 25%, slightly improving his ability to land lucky air-shots. A highly skilled Junkrat might also attempt to use his Concussion Mine to launch himself into the skybox to meet Pharah mid-air. If he is running the Bomb Voyage perk, doing this grants him a 35% attack speed boost for 3 seconds, allowing him to rapidly spam grenades during his ascent. Pharah should simply use Jet Dash to maintain distance and shoot him while his movement is locked into a predictable ballistic arc.
matchups.synergy:
A Junkrat and Pharah combination (often referred to as "Spam Comp") outputs the highest amount of continuous explosive damage in the game. This composition completely invalidates grounded, barrier-heavy Tank compositions (such as Reinhardt or Sigma) by instantly melting their shields and flooding choke points with unavoidable splash damage.

While this composition leaves the team highly vulnerable to enemy hitscans or Echo, it is unparalleled at breaking bunker defenses. Junkrat's Steel Trap also provides excellent utility for Pharah; an immobilized enemy is guaranteed to take two direct Rocket Launcher hits, ensuring a fast and effortless execution.

matchups.matchup:
Mei's primary fire, the Endothermic Blaster, has a maximum range of 10 meters, making it completely useless against an airborne Pharah. However, Pharah must respect Mei's secondary fire. The Icicle is a fast-moving (115 m/s) projectile that deals 85 body damage and 170 damage on a critical hit. A precise Mei can easily snipe a Pharah who is hovering predictably.

Because Mei possesses incredible stalling tools with Cryo-Freeze and Ice Wall, she is generally a low-priority target; Pharah's time is better spent pressuring vulnerable Supports. Be especially cautious of diving a low-health Mei if she has equipped the Cryo-Storm Major Perk. This perk causes her Cryo-Freeze to deal 70 damage per second and apply a severe slow to anyone within 4.5 meters, heavily punishing Pharah if she attempts to secure a close-range execution while Mei is encased.

If Mei equips the Glacial Propulsion Minor Perk, she gains the ability to double jump and spawn a small ice pillar that launches her 6.5 meters into the air. While this gives her surprising vertical mobility to dodge rockets or seek better Icicle angles, her trajectory becomes highly predictable on the descent.
matchups.synergy:
Mei provides phenomenal setup utility for Pharah's explosive arsenal. Ice Wall can physically split the enemy team, cutting off Tanks from their Supports and trapping them in confined spaces where Pharah's splash damage is inescapable.

Mei's Ultimate, Blizzard, is one of the best combo tools for Barrage. Once enemies are frozen solid, Pharah can safely descend and unleash her ultimate without fear of being stunned or interrupted. If Mei is running the Skating Rink Minor Perk, the interior of the Blizzard becomes a massive safe zone, providing Pharah with a 25% speed boost and 50 health per second, allowing her to safely drop out of the sky for quick healing.

matchups.matchup:
Engaging in an aerial dogfight with an enemy Pharah is notoriously inefficient. Because both heroes rely on slow-moving projectiles and erratic aerial mobility, attempting to land direct hits mid-air often wastes valuable time and ammo. In most scenarios, it is tactically superior to ignore the enemy Pharah and focus on bombarding her grounded Supports.

However, if you must engage, closing the distance is key. Use Jump Jet and Jet Dash to get directly in her face to guarantee your rocket impacts. Be highly aware of her loadout: if the enemy Pharah has equipped the Helix Shields Minor Perk, she will convert 125 health into shields that regenerate on direct hits, making her exceptionally tanky. If she is running the Rocket Salvo Major Perk, she becomes significantly more dangerous in air-to-air combat, as using her movement abilities will alter her next primary fire into two spiraling mini-rockets that are much easier to land on a hovering target.

Lastly, be mindful of the Recon Sub-Role passive. If you fall below 50% health, the enemy Pharah will be able to see your exact silhouette through walls for 5 seconds, making it impossible to hide and regenerate safely.
matchups.synergy:
A duplicate Pharah composition completely overwhelms the enemy team's anti-air resources. Most team compositions only possess one or two hitscan heroes; forcing them to simultaneously track two highly mobile airborne threats usually results in the hitscans being quickly overwhelmed and eliminated.

The combined splash damage of two Rocket Launchers will instantly obliterate grouped enemies and rapidly shatter standard Tank barriers. Furthermore, triggering the Recon passive allows both Pharahs to perfectly coordinate their dives, tracking low-health targets through walls and securing instant, cross-map executions.

matchups.matchup:
Reaper is traditionally helpless against a well-positioned Pharah. The severe damage falloff and wide spread of his Hellfire Shotguns render him practically useless against targets high in the skybox. Pharah can freely bombard his large hitbox from a distance, frequently forcing him to burn Wraith Form just to survive.

However, Pharah must remain highly vigilant if Reaper equips the Dire Triggers Major Perk. This fundamentally alters his threat level, allowing him to fire a concentrated secondary volley from both shotguns with a significantly extended falloff range (up to 35 meters). This hitscan blast can deal surprising burst damage to a hovering Pharah, making him far more dangerous than his standard kit implies.

If Reaper attempts to use Shadow Step to reach Pharah's high ground, she can easily displace him mid-animation with a well-timed Concussive Blast, dropping him back into her team's line of fire. His Death Blossom ultimate poses absolutely zero threat to an airborne Pharah, allowing her to effortlessly execute him while his movement speed is crippled.
matchups.synergy:
Reaper and Pharah operate on completely different planes of engagement, meaning they rarely interact directly. However, they effectively split the enemy's defensive attention. Reaper's lethal close-quarters presence demands the immediate focus of the enemy Tanks on the ground, which naturally creates the space Pharah needs to operate unpressured in the sky.

If Reaper equips the Lingering Wraith Minor Perk (granting a 40% movement speed boost upon exiting Wraith Form), he can easily run down and execute the vulnerable targets that Pharah physically displaces out from behind enemy barriers using her Concussive Blast.

matchups.matchup:
As a Recon hero equipped with tracking munitions, Sierra is an existential threat to Pharah. While her Helix Rifle naturally tightens its spread under sustained fire (made even faster by the Tight Grip Minor Perk), the true danger lies in her Tracking Shot. If Pharah is marked by this dart, Sierra's primary fire will automatically curve and track Pharah through the air. Because aerial evasion is completely useless against tracking bullets, Pharah must immediately use Jet Dash to drop behind hard environmental cover until the 5-second mark expires.

Do not assume you are safe simply because you are high up. Sierra's Anchor Drone allows her to grapple vertically to directly contest the skybox, a threat heavily amplified if she uses the Full Flight Minor Perk to increase her grapple range by 25%. If Sierra equips the Locked In Major Perk, successfully marking Pharah grants her an immediate 20% attack speed boost, melting Pharah out of the sky almost instantly. Pharah must utilize stealthy flanks to ambush Sierra, securing two quick direct hits before the Tracking Shot can be cast.
matchups.synergy:
Sierra provides exceptional target acquisition and displacement utility for Pharah. Because Sierra's Recon Sub-Role passive reveals enemies below 50% health through walls, Pharah is constantly fed wall-hack intelligence, allowing her to perfectly pre-fire her slow-moving rockets at retreating targets.

Additionally, Sierra's Tremor Charge and Trailblazer ultimate both forcefully displace enemies from entrenched positions. When Sierra carpet-bombs a linear path, the enemy team is forced to scatter into predictable evasive maneuvers, setting up incredibly easy direct hits for Pharah's Rocket Launcher or a devastating Barrage.

matchups.matchup:
Sojourn is arguably one of the most lethal anti-air heroes in the game. While her primary fire is projectile-based, she uses it to farm energy off Pharah's grounded Tanks or barriers, only to instantly turn her hitscan Charged Shot on Pharah for a devastating execution. Much like Hanzo, Sojourn benefits from the Sharpshooter passive, meaning landing critical hits will rapidly refund her Power Slide, making her quite difficult to pin down.

Pharah must track Sojourn's energy glow carefully. Do not hover in the open if her Railgun is fully charged. Be particularly wary if she equips the Friction Generators Major Perk. With this perk, Sojourn generates up to 50 energy simply by sliding, meaning she no longer needs to farm your team to prepare a lethal shot against you. If she instead uses the Dual Thrusters perk, she gains two slide charges, granting her unparalleled mobility.

Her Ultimate, Overclock, is a definitive death sentence for an airborne Pharah. Because the energy auto-charges, she can continuously fire piercing hitscan shots. If she is utilizing the Overcharged Minor Perk, her maximum energy capacity increases to 150, allowing her to deal up to 170 body damage (or 255 headshot damage) in a single blast. Dropping out of the sky into hard cover is the only viable survival strategy.
matchups.synergy:
Sojourn and Pharah create a perfect synergy of area denial and execution. Sojourn's Disruptor Shot traps enemies in a localized damage-over-time sphere. Enemies caught inside must immediately walk out of it, making their movement highly predictable and setting them up perfectly for Pharah's Rocket Launcher direct hits.

Conversely, Pharah's massive splash damage routinely softens up the enemy backline, providing Sojourn with a plethora of weakened targets that she can effortlessly finish off from across the map using her Charged Shot.

matchups.matchup:
Soldier: 76 is one of Pharah's most notorious counters, and understandably, can easily convince you to switch heroes. You should treat Soldier: 76 as a primary threat and outplay him through unpredictability. His Heavy Pulse Rifle is a hitscan weapon that can consistently chip away Pharah's health while she is airborne. To engage him successfully, Pharah must utilize environmental cover to close the gap unspotted, then quickly dive him using a combination of Jump Jet and Jet Dash to secure two direct Rocket Launcher hits before he can react.

Be highly mindful of his Biotic Field, which allows him to out-sustain your splash damage. If he deploys it, use Concussive Blast to physically knock him out of its healing radius. Note that if he has equipped the Stim Pack Major Perk, he sacrifices his AoE field for a selfish heal and a 20% attack speed buff; do not attempt a sustained duel against this, as his increased DPS will melt Pharah out of the sky. His Helix Rockets are also a major threat if Pharah hovers predictably, especially if he is running the Helix Propulsion Minor Perk, which makes the rockets 50% faster and much harder to dodge mid-air.

Soldier's Ultimate, Tactical Visor, is effectively a death sentence for an exposed Pharah. The moment the voice line is heard, Pharah must immediately drop out of the sky or use Jet Dash to reach hard cover. If he has the Tactical Salvo perk, his Helix Rockets' cooldown is reduced to 1.2 seconds during the Ultimate, making him incredibly lethal even if you manage to break his auto-aim line of sight.
matchups.synergy: Soldier: 76 and Pharah apply pressure from completely different vectors. While Pharah forces the enemy team to look up and deal with massive projectile splash damage, Soldier: 76 can freely lay down consistent hitscan fire from horizontal off-angles. This splits the enemy's defensive resources and makes it difficult for Tanks to mitigate both sources of damage simultaneously. Additionally, a grounded Soldier: 76 can drop his Biotic Field behind cover to provide Pharah with a localized healing station if her Supports are otherwise occupied.

matchups.matchup:
Sombra dictates engagements entirely on her terms and poses a severe threat to a hovering Pharah. If Sombra manages to Hack Pharah out of the sky, it immediately disables Hover Jets, Jump Jet, and Jet Dash, sending Pharah plummeting helplessly into the enemy team. Landing out of position usually results in a quick death, especially since Sombra's Virus and Opportunist passive deal devastating burst damage specifically to hacked targets.

Pharah must play with extreme paranoia if Sombra is using the Encrypted Upload Minor Perk. This allows Sombra to initiate a Hack without fully breaking stealth, meaning Pharah cannot easily react and shoot her with splash damage to interrupt the cast. If Sombra lands a Virus on a hacked target while using the Viral Replication Major Perk, the damage-over-time will aggressively spread to anyone within 8 meters, severely punishing Pharah if she attempts to drop down near her grounded Supports for safety.

Sombra's ultimate, EMP, operates on a massive spherical radius that can easily reach Pharah in the sky. If Sombra uses Translocator to throw herself into the air before EMPing, Pharah must immediately drop behind high-ground cover to avoid being hacked and grounded.
matchups.synergy:
Sombra is the ultimate enabler for an aggressive Pharah. A coordinated Sombra can Hack an enemy hitscan (like Soldier: 76 or Ashe) or a protective Tank (like D.Va), completely removing Pharah's primary counters from the equation before she initiates a dive.

Additionally, the combination of EMP completely stripping enemy barriers and locking out defensive cooldowns, followed instantly by Pharah's Barrage, is one of the most reliable and devastating team-wiping combos in the game.

matchups.matchup:
Symmetra relies entirely on her close-range Photon Projector beam and stationary Sentry Turrets, rendering her practically helpless against a high-flying Pharah. Pharah can effortlessly clear Symmetra's turrets from a safe distance using splash damage. Because Symmetra's alternate fire projectiles are relatively slow and require charging, she will rarely land a shot on an unpredictably hovering Pharah.

While Symmetra is a low-priority target for Pharah personally, she should be focused if she is actively melting your grounded Tanks. Be mindful of her equipped perks; if she runs the Perfect Alignment Minor Perk, her primary fire beam reaches 14.4 meters, slightly increasing her anti-air threat if Pharah flies too low. If Symmetra equips the Shield Battery Major Perk, she regenerates 20 shields per second while standing near her Teleporter, making her surprisingly resilient to splash damage and requiring Pharah to commit to direct hits to secure the elimination.
matchups.synergy: Symmetra and Pharah do not naturally synergize in their neutral game, as Pharah rarely benefits from the grounded mobility of the Teleporter. However, Symmetra's ultimate, Photon Barrier, provides unparalleled aerial cover. Pharah can weave back and forth across the massive 4000-health barrier mid-air, allowing her to rain down rockets or unleash a highly exposed Barrage with complete invulnerability from enemy hitscans. If Symmetra equips the Hovering Barrier Major Perk, she can create a forward-moving shield instead, providing dynamic cover for Pharah to push forward aggressively.

matchups.matchup:
Torbjörn's Deploy Turret has a 40-meter auto-lock radius that will continuously harass Pharah, making it impossible for her to remain in the skybox without taking constant chip damage. Pharah is uniquely equipped to dismantle this turret by corner-peeking and firing Rocket Launcher projectiles from behind cover. The turret is the true priority; once it is destroyed, Torbjörn himself is a low-threat target, as his arcing Rivet Gun projectiles are difficult to land on a flying enemy.

Pharah must be extremely cautious if Torbjörn equips the Overloaded Turret Major Perk. When he activates Overload, the turret instantly gains 150 health and fires devastating 30-damage missile bursts every 1.5 seconds, turning it into a lethal anti-air installation. Pharah must break line of sight until the 5-second upgrade expires. Additionally, the Anchor Bolts Major Perk allows him to place the turret on ceilings and high walls, which can catch Pharah off guard and negate her usual splash-damage angles.
matchups.synergy:
Torbjörn and Pharah create a highly effective split-pressure crossfire. While Pharah attacks from the sky, Torbjörn's Deploy Turret provides consistent, automated hitscan pressure on the ground. This forces the enemy team to constantly choose between looking up to deal with Pharah or turning around to destroy the turret.

Torbjörn's Molten Core ultimate covers the objective in deadly slag, forcing grounded enemies to look down and carefully navigate the hazard. Pharah can easily exploit this distracted movement to land direct rocket hits on targets trying to escape the molten pools.

matchups.matchup:
Tracer's extremely short effective range (10 to 20 meters) and wide weapon spread mean she poses almost no threat to a Pharah operating at optimal altitude. Pharah can freely bombard the enemy backline from the skybox while largely ignoring her. However, hitting Tracer with Rocket Launcher projectiles is exceedingly difficult due to her erratic Blink mobility. Landing a splash hit will usually force out her Recall, which removes her from the fight temporarily and creates an advantage for your team.

Be mindful of her perk loadout. If she equips the Quantum Entanglement Major Perk, she will emerge from Recall with 50 overhealth, allowing her to survive what would normally be a lethal direct rocket hit. Additionally, if she has the Chronal Dash Minor Perk, her Blinks cover 9 meters instead of 7.5, requiring you to lead your projectiles significantly further to predict her movement.

If Tracer manages to stick Pharah with her Pulse Bomb, it is often best to use Jump Jet to propel yourself as far away from your airborne Supports as possible before it detonates, minimizing collateral damage.
matchups.synergy: Tracer and Pharah form a highly effective split-dive duo. Pharah's massive splash damage routinely softens up the enemy backline, leaving them highly vulnerable to a quick execution from Tracer's Pulse Pistols. Furthermore, the constant aerial bombardment forces enemies to look upward and burn defensive cooldowns, allowing Tracer to freely navigate the ground and secure Pulse Bomb sticks unbothered.

matchups.matchup:
Vendetta is a melee-centric Flanker who fundamentally struggles to interact with a high-flying Pharah. Her Palatine Fang and Sundering Blade ultimate require close-quarters engagement, allowing Pharah to rain down rockets with near impunity. When bombarding her, aim your Rocket Launcher slightly behind her to bypass her Warding Stance, which only reduces damage from the front.

However, Pharah must remain vigilant if flying low or navigating tight map geometry. Vendetta can use Soaring Slice to hurl her sword up to 15 meters into the air and instantly teleport to it, potentially striking Pharah with a lethal Overhead Strike mid-air. Hitting her becomes exceptionally difficult if she is running the Relentless Major Perk; the drastically increased movement speed from stacking 8 Onslaught buffs makes her highly evasive.
matchups.synergy:
Vendetta and Pharah excel at overwhelming grounded Tanks and Supports from entirely different angles. While Pharah forces the enemy team to look upward and scatter to avoid splash damage, Vendetta utilizes her extreme melee mobility to isolate and execute the fleeing targets.

Since Vendetta has immense self-sustain through her Siphoning Strike Major Perk and the Flanker sub-role passive, she operates highly independently. This means Pharah's Supports (such as Mercy or Jetpack Cat) are completely free to pocket her in the skybox without leaving the ground team vulnerable.

matchups.matchup:
Under normal circumstances, Pharah heavily counters Venture. Venture's Smart Excavator projectiles automatically detonate after just 16 meters, and their ultimate, Tectonic Shock, is entirely grounded, sending shockwaves exclusively along the floor. By simply maintaining altitude with Hover Jets, Pharah remains completely immune to Venture's entire base kit. When Venture uses Burrow to gain invulnerability, Pharah can hover directly above them and perfectly time a rocket for the exact moment they emerge.

The dynamic shifts drastically if Venture equips the Smart Extender Major Perk. Activating this perk temporarily doubles their primary fire range to 32 meters, allowing them to easily hit Pharah in the skybox with explosive projectiles. Pharah must monitor Venture's cooldowns and immediately seek high-ground cover or drop altitude if this perk is activated to avoid being bursted out of the air.
matchups.synergy:
Venture dominates enclosed spaces and low-ceiling areas, while Pharah controls the open skies. This forces the enemy team into a lose-lose situation: if they step out into the open, Pharah bombards them; if they retreat indoors for cover, Venture effortlessly sweeps them with Drill Dash and Tectonic Shock.

Additionally, Venture's Burrow emergence forcefully knocks enemies upward into predictable vertical arcs. A skilled Pharah can easily capitalize on this crowd control, setting up guaranteed, mid-air direct hits with her Rocket Launcher.

matchups.matchup:
Widowmaker is Pharah's natural predator, but only when the conditions meet. A skilled Widowmaker will find the time to snipe you while you may be out in midair focusing somebody else, so she can become a big threat if left unchecked.

A fully-charged headshot from Widow's Kiss can instantly eliminate Pharah, but an experienced Pharah can effectively turn Widowmaker into a sitting duck. Because Widowmaker suffers a severe 65% movement speed penalty while aiming down sights, she is highly vulnerable to incoming projectile fire. By utilizing unpredictable aerial momentum and using complex rooftop geometry to flank unseen, Pharah can easily bombard Widowmaker's sniper nest with Rocket Launcher direct hits to secure a quick elimination, or even a use of Concussive Blast to force her out of position.

Diving Widowmaker directly still requires caution. If she is using the Sniper's Instinct Minor Perk, she can use her Grappling Hook to evade Pharah's bombardment, which grants her a 100% faster charge rate on her scoped shots for 2 seconds. This allows her to quickly counter-snipe Pharah mid-air. Furthermore, the Widow's Bite Major Perk allows her shots to charge to 125%, dealing a massive 375 damage on a headshot—completely ignoring any minor overhealth or pocket healing Pharah might be receiving.

Be wary of her Venom Mine when flanking her perch. If she has equipped the Seeker Mine Major Perk, the mine will actively fire poison darts at Pharah within a 10-meter radius rather than requiring a proximity trigger, applying a damage-over-time effect and revealing Pharah's flank to the enemy team through walls.
matchups.synergy:
Widowmaker's sheer presence forces the enemy team to hide behind environmental cover or clump together behind tank barriers to avoid her sightlines. Pharah thrives against tightly clustered enemies, using her Rocket Launcher splash damage to punish teams trying to hide from the sniper.

Widowmaker's Ultimate, Infra-Sight, provides Pharah with invaluable information. Knowing exactly where the enemy is moving behind walls allows Pharah to pre-fire her slow-moving rockets for guaranteed direct hits as enemies round corners, or to perfectly time her Jump Jet to flank the backline for an unreactable Barrage.

matchups.matchup: You have to land two direct shots with catch her off guard as fast as possible. Otherwise, Juno have All THE TOOLS SHE NEED to defeat you. As you're more often to miss your shot because her flying movement (Lift Off Perk make her even harder to hit). And her hitscan plus Pulsar Torpedoes will always hit you unless you have to find cover (Faster Blaster Perk make her remove you even more faster with automatic shot). Overall Juno is very bad matchup for Pharah.

comments: The Vengeful Vortex perk significantly improved the flexibility of Ravenous Vortex, especially when interacting with airborne targets. That functionality has been added to the base ability with reduced damage. Prolonged Barrier returns as a Minor Perk option, and Void Surge has been buffed and moved to a Major Perk.

Damage per second increased from 30 to 35.

comments: Reducing Void Barrier’s cooldown improves its cycling within engagements, while increasing Annihilation’s damage per second enhances its presence during extended fights.

changes.text: Base health increased from 250 to 275
No longer has half effectiveness while in Annihilation

comments: Previous changes led to a healthier overall playstyle for Ramattra, but he could feel too fragile in certain matchups. Increasing his base health improves survivability in both forms.

Bonus armor increased from 200 to 225. (undocumented) [verify]

comments: Developer Comments: Ramattra has become too durable in Nemesis Form while blocking. The armor and Block adjustments reduce his ability to withstand large amounts of damage and force more deliberate defensive choices. The change to Ravenous Vortex removes the jarring stop in horizontal momentum, notably when paired with Vengeful Vortex.

changes.text: Healing per second increased from 50 to 75.

comments: Developer Comments: Nanite Repair’s healing per second has been increased to enhance its consistency and overall effectiveness during the short duration of Ravenous Vortex.

changes.text: Now additionally increases the size of the Void Barrier by 25%.

comments: Developer Comments: An additional element has been added to Prolonged Barrier to enable Ramattra to control a larger area and provide effective cover with the shield.

comments: Developer Comment: Ramattra has been underperforming relative to other brawl tanks. Adding a small increase to his armor will provide a necessary boost without altering his core gameplay.

changes.text: Reverted to pierce barriers again.
No longer deals critical damage to barriers.
No longer pierces barriers.
Now deals 2.5x more damage to barriers.

comments: Developer Comments: Ramattra's Pummel projectiles passing through barriers was a source of frustration for players trying to protect themselves or their allies. With these changes enabling Ramattra to deal critical damage to barriers, he will still be a valuable hero choice against barrier mechanics, but won't immediately apply damage to players on the other side.

Base armor reduced from 100 to 75.
Base health reduced from 275 to 250.
Bonus armor increased from 225 to 300.
Pummel damage increased from 60 to 65.

comments: Developer Comments: The Pummel damage adjustment is notable as it reduces the number of punches required to knockout a 250 health hero.

comments: Developer Comments: Ramattra is quite powerful during his Nemesis Form though his base Omnic Form may be too easy to ignore for a tank hero. We're adding some power there to even out the tradeoffs between the two forms, with the Omnic Form having even better ranged damage while Nemesis Form’s Pummel can pierce enemy defenses.

changes.text: Cooldown decreased from 8 to 7 seconds.

comments: Developer Comments: This change lets Ramattra project his influence more frequently with Nemesis Form, which translates into increased survivability and damage. The flexibility also makes it less punishing if he swaps back to Omnic Form early to use the Void Barrier.

changes.text: Block now reduces damage from stuck projectiles.
Ultimate cost increased 12%.
Block now reduces damage from stuck projectiles.

comments: Developer Comments: Similar to Doomfist’s Power Block change, Ramattra’s Block ability will now always apply damage reduction to projectiles stuck directly to him. His Annihilation ultimate ability was being generated slightly too quickly for how impactful it can be, so we are increasing its ultimate cost.

changes.text: The projectile now passes through enemy heroes but is still blocked by barriers.

comments: Developer Comments: Sometimes, the Ravenous Vortex projectile hits an enemy and bounces off unpredictably, delaying its activation. This quality-of-life change improves the ability's consistency and makes it easier to use against groups of enemies without fear of accidental collisions.

changes.text: Using Annihilation while in Nemesis Form refreshes your bonus armor

comments: Developer Comment: Players found that shifting out of Nemesis Form before activating the Annihilation ultimate would fully reset Nemesis Form's bonus armor. To smooth out the gameplay, it now resets the armor health automatically as part of the ultimate activation.

changes.text: Base health in Role Queue modes remains the same at 450

comments: Developer Comment: Developer Comment: The idea of an ultimate ability potentially lasting forever is an exciting concept, but the reality is that if it's too easy to do it causes a lot of frustrations and with Ramattra's ultimate in particular, an excessive amount of visual noise. We're limiting the maximum duration to 20 seconds, which is still highly impactful for most team fights, but it guarantees it'll end in a reasonable amount of time.

matchups.matchup: D.VA's Fusion Cannons deal negligible damage at long range, unlike your Void Accelerator. However, Defense Matrix can destroy the nanites emitted from your staff. D.Va will have to charge at you with Boosters to deal greater. Now, you can turn the tables on her. Once she close, switch to Nemesis Form and D.Va has no defenses against your punches besides fleeing. If D.Va uses Self-Destruct, either your Void Barrier or Block (during Nemesis form) are viable defenses against it.

If you see Doomfist approaching, use your Ravenous Vortex to slow him down (or pull him down early if engaging with Seismic Slam). Avoid pummeling him when he uses Power Block as three punches will empower his next Rocket Punch. Use Block to reduce the damage from Meteor Strike, or use Ravenous Vortex, to slow him down once his ultimate ends.

Mauga will be a pain in your side. Due to your hitbox, especially in Nemesis Form, he can set you ablaze with Incendiary Chaingun. Once burning, he can inflict critical hits with his Volatile Chaingun. Your only means of defense against this is your Void Barrier, and even then, it's temporary. While Block does provide damage reduction, Mauga's high rate of fire can still chip away much of your health. Also, Overrun is ignores your slowing effect and the stomp and can knock up down, inflicting even more damage. Cage Fight can make things worse for you as once you're trapped, you can't escape and Mauga can just focus fire you with his guns. Be sure to play around natural cover and have supports around to keep you up.

Don't engage Orisa too early. Stay back and wait for Orisa to burn her cooldowns first before engaging. Javelin Spin blocks your Pummel, Energy Javelin can push you back, and you deal less damage while Fortify is active. When she uses Terra Surge, your Block greatly reduces the damage you receive. However, if you see Orisa charging with Javelin Spin, use your Void Barrier to block her.

In a 1-on-1 scenario, you want to be the second person to use Nemesis Form. If the enemy Ramattra uses Annihilation first, use your Void Barrier to block the nanites and fall back. Use Ravenous Vortex to slow him down as he will certainly charge towards you. Remember, Annihilation ends after three seconds of no damage.

Never enter a battle against a Reinhardt when you're not in your Nemesis Form. All it takes for him to dispatch you out is one successful Charge and one strike of his Rocket Hammer, and just like that, you'll be waiting for a respawn after just a matter of seconds. If you are being charged by a Reinhardt, alert your team to pocket you to keep yourself safe and remain in the fight for longer, or if you can react quickly, enter your Nemesis Form to make use of your added armor.


On your side, if you want to take him down, enter your Nemesis Form whenever you can. Not only you'll bypass his barrier and damage it, but you'll deal some damage to Reinhardt himself (and any of his allies behind him). This allows your team to then concentrate fire on Reinhardt and take him out quickly with a large group of forces. Also, Reinhardt is mostly limited to close range so staying outside of his hammer swing range (5 m) gives you the upper hand.

Void Barrier can block his Chain Hook and it can interrupt his hook combo by placing it between him and a hook ally. Do not use Nemesis Form (and by extension, Annihilation) against Whole Hog. Whole Hog can push you back, so far back that your nanites can't reach anyone or off the map. Wait for his ultimate to end or Roadhog's death before using either ability.

You have the upper hand against Sigma. Your weapon has no range limit. Plus, simply shield aggressively to close to distance and quickly switch to Nemesis Form. Neither Experimental Barrier nor Kinetic Grasp can block Pummel. All Sigma can do is use Accretion and follow up with his Hyperspheres. As long as your being healed by support, you can keep going until he's in back in the respawn room. Caution with Gravitic Flux as you have no way of blocking the slam damage.

Wrecking Ball health pool means you probably can't deal meaningful damage to him. Your Void Barrier can block his Piledriver damage. Ravenous Vortex can be used to slow him down or pull down. Realistically, since Wrecking Ball will most definitely go after your backline, follow suit and go after his backline.

If Winston dives your backline, place Void Barrier in front of his support so he can't be healed. Run in with Nemesis Form and Pummel him. After 3-4 punches, place Ravenous Vortex to close off his escape.

Force Zarya to use her barriers early as without them, she's relatively easier to eliminate. Your Void Barrier can block most of her damage. Once she's used both of her barriers, throw down a Ravenous Vortex and charge at her in Nemesis Form.

matchups.matchup: Aside from poking with your Void Accelerator and occasionally throwing Ravenous Vortex at her from a distance, there is not much you can do against a properly positioned Ashe as her Dynamite can go over your Void Barrier and damage you and your team. At close range, try to keep damaging her until she uses her Coach Gun then chase her down with Ravenous Vortex or your Nemesis form.

Hide behind walls and use natural cover against a Bastion in Assault configuration. Your Void Barrier and Power Block are ineffective against Bastion as he can still melt you through it, and they should only be used to escort you to cover or as your last-resort defense. When Bastion is not in Assault, his relatively large hitbox is easy to damage with your Void Accelerator, so take advantage of it to kill him or bait out Assault.

Cassidy is as good as dead if you catch him at close range with your Nemesis form - however still be cautious as he can fan fire you at close range and slow you down with his Flashbang which will make it harder for you to close the distance with him. Utilize your Void Barrier and Ravenous Vortex well to counteract this.

You are not well-equipped to deal with flying heroes. Try to throw a Ravenous Vortex at an Echo that does not have Flight or is not looking at you, as she might avoid your abilities before she can be caught by them. If Echo duplicates you during her ultimate, use your Void Barrier to sever off any healing she might get and pummel her with Nemesis form before she can get her ultimate ready.

If a Genji is harassing your team, pummel him with your Nemesis form or throw a Ravenous Vortex at him. This will either kill or scare him into using Swift Strike or Deflect, essentially ending his turn meaning that he will be unable to dive your team. Your ultimate is also a decent counter to his Dragonblade as your ultimate can pierce through his Deflect.

A good Hanzo will often stay away from you as much as possible or stand on areas you cannot access easily. Hanzo has little mobility to get himself out - exploit this. Cut off his sightlines with Void Barrier, use Ravenous Vortex and pummel him with your Nemesis form to secure a kill whenever possible.
With Block from your Nemesis Form, you should be able to survive Dragonstrike as you will take significantly less damage over time.

It is extremely risky to fight a Junkrat at close range without your Nemesis form as he has higher burst damage than your Void Accelerator and can kill you if you're not careful. Junkrat can be slippery to fight as he can place a Steel Trap while running away or throw a Concussion Mine at you to create distance between you and him. Do note that a Junkrat stuck in your Ravenous Vortex is usually an easy kill as he is unable to escape while being stuck in the vortex.

Try to save Void Barrier or Nemesis form in your ability reserve if you know Mei is alive. She can wall you off from your team, but either of the cooldowns mentioned before can greatly increase your chances of living until your team can break the wall behind you, whether you shield yourself or Power Block the damage. Pummel her with your Nemesis form to force her to use Cryo Freeze and she should easily be eliminated.
matchups.synergy: Mei has good synergy with Ramattra. Ice Wall can cutoff enemies' escape routes, making it easier for you to hunt down while in Nemesis Form. Her Blizzard can be comboed with your ultimate, as frozen enemies cannot fight back against Nemesis Form or Annihiation.

matchups.matchup: Pharah will rarely play within your range, so it is best to ignore her while she is in the air for your team to deal with. In the case that she is vulnerable, Ravenous Vortex can help your team secure a kill onto Pharah to prevent her from flying away. Keep track of her ultimate as her Barrage can kill you through your Power Block. Play near cover accordingly.

Void Barrier easily denies Reaper from doing any damage onto you and hence makes him easy to ignore while you are fighting. If you are directly confronting a Reaper, place down a Void Barrier first then enter Nemesis form to kill him or force him into using Wraith.

Sojourn can be extremely slippery as her Power Slide can get her out in many scenarios where you are fighting her. Use Ravenous Vortex to lower the odds of her getting away. She will often use a Disruptor Shot when you are behind a Void Barrier, so either utilize natural cover or trust your supports to heal you through it. Rush her down with your Nemesis form when she has no Power Slide.

Most of the time, Sombra does not pose a threat to you as she will usually be focusing the rest of your team instead. However in situations where she may focus on you, she will usually Hack you in your Nemesis form to stop you from using Power Block. This will not matter most of the time as Hack lasts for a short time and your defensive abilities (aside from Power Block) cannot be cancelled by Hack. Try not to waste any abilities such as Ravenous Vortex or Nemesis against a Sombra as she will run away and your Void Accelerator usually suffices as enough damage to scare her into doing so.

Barriers are fuel for Symmetra's primary fire, so it is better to enter Nemesis form straight away and start pummeling her. You will always outdamage a Symmetra at close range regardless of her charge with Nemesis form so focus her if she becomes aggressive immediately.

Hitting a Tracer is difficult with your Void Accelerator and she can easily escape your Ravenous Vortex with Blink. In this matchup, you want to get near Tracer to kill her instantly before she can react (with two Nemesis form punches and a quick melee on the second punch) or force her to Recall as soon as possible. Without Nemesis form, it's hard for you to secure a kill on a Tracer by yourself so coordinate with your team to deal with her.

Widowmaker will usually be staying far away from the fight and on the high ground, which makes it difficult for you to deal with her. Use Void Barrier and natural cover whenever possible to minimize the damage she does onto you and your team. Keep in mind that she has Grappling Hook and try to save your abilities accordingly to chase her down.

matchups.matchup: Ana's Biotic Grenade and Sleep Dart can pose a decent threat against you. She will typically throw her Biotic Grenade during fights to give her team the upper hand, so save Void Barrier or Nemesis form for this. Her Sleep Dart can also shut down your ultimate, so be cautious and wait for Ana to use her Sleep Dart first then use ultimate.
matchups.synergy: The combined power of a Nano Boost and Annihilation is incredible. Make the full use of this ultimate combo, and you'll blitz enemy teams, with your added power. A friendly Ana can also halt enemies from trying to pursue you down with the use of her Sleep Dart, such as putting a charging Reinhart to a stop. Synchronize your attacks to make the most out of this combination.

matchups.matchup: Baptiste's damage and Immortality Field can make some of your engagements more difficult, but otherwise his kit should not be a major problem to you. Catch him with a Ravenous Vortex so that he cannot use his Exo Boots to jump to a safe place. Baptiste's Amplification Matrix can kill you within less than a few seconds if you are not careful. Play behind cover when you hear Baptiste's cue for his ultimate, or directly contest him with your Nemesis form if you are close enough to him.
matchups.synergy:
Since you're a ground hero, it's easier for Baptiste to sustain you in close-range brawls. His Immortality Field can keep you up when your health becomes dangerously low.
Amplification Matrix can double the damage of almost all of your damage. However, despite the added power to your Pummel strikes, it's rarely useful due to the ultimate's stationary nature.

matchups.matchup: At long range, she can absorb your nanites with her shield to her benefit, giving her health. However, at close range her shield does little to protect her from pummel and quick melee. Be careful, as once her shield is down her attacks are strongest at close range. The good news is, outside of her shield bash, she has little in ways of movement- so once she is in range of your nemesis form or ultimate, it can be difficult for her to escape.

First thing is almost always to take down her pylon, which can be incredibly fast and easy to do with your nanites. This will also prevent her from self healing. Her main attack ability is long range, so you have little to lose by pummeling her close range. She can use her jump ability do defend herself and escape her pummel, so it's ideal to wait until she's used her jump before pummeling her.
Juno  can be slippery for you. Her Glide Boost and/or Hyper Ring can give her the speed to dodge your attacks at close range.
matchups.synergy: Hyper Ring can speed up Ramattra in Nemesis Form, making it easier to hunt down enemies trying to flee. Orbital Ray can also be greatly helpful as it simultaneously heals and damage boosts him. Combo it with Annihilation and cleave your enemies with your empowered punches and damage over time.

matchups.matchup: Kiriko does very minimal damage against you as Ramattra, so her damage does not pose any threat against you, but her abilities and ultimate should always be dealt with first. When you directly confront a Kiriko, it is likely that she has her Swift Step or Protection Suzu ready so use as little cooldowns as possible to force her to use them first, then go after her or any of her other teammates after you have forced her to use either of her cooldowns. The key in this matchup is to use Ravenous Vortex after she has expended her abilities so that she has no way of escaping and can be secured as an easy kill. Do be careful of her Kitsune Rush as her team can run you down very easily with it even with your defensive abilities, and it is wise to kite it, then play near your team and wait it out before re-engaging.

Dealing with Mercy is very similar to Pharah and Echo, do not focus her too hard as she will typically be playing in the backlines and in the sky, out of your effective range. As usual, use Ravenous Vortex when she is vulnerable, but specifically look for when she uses her Guardian Angel flight, throwing one at her as soon as she has performed her second "jump" in her flight. This ensures that you will not miss your vortex because she flew away.

Ramattra's matchup with Moira is similar to Kiriko in the sense that you should use minimal, and if you can, no abilities to force her to use her own defensive abilities and then catch her or her teammates out when she's in a state of vulnerability.  Moira's damage, even with her Biotic Orb and Coalescence is typically insignificant against you in your Nemesis form, but you should still pummel her to scare her away before she can do any more healing or damage with it.

Discord Orb can spell death for you if you are not careful. Always make sure you are playing near cover when you know there is a Zenyatta on the enemy team to get the Discord Orb off you, then try and isolate him from his team with your Nemesis form and Ravenous Vortex to dispatch him as quickly as possible.

wiki.name: Reaper
wiki.description: Some speak of a black-robed terrorist known only as the Reaper. His identity and motives are a mystery. What is known is that where he appears, death follows.

abilities.name: Hellfire Shotguns
abilities.description: Short-range spread weapons.

abilities.name: Shadow Step
abilities.description: Teleport to a targeted location.

abilities.name: Wraith Form
abilities.description: Move faster and become invulnerable, but you cannot shoot.

abilities.name: Death Blossom
abilities.description: Damage all nearby enemies.

abilities.name: The Reaping
abilities.description: Dealing damage heals you.

perks.name: Lingering Wraith
perks.description: Leaving Wraith Form grants 30% movement speed for 2 seconds.

perks.name: Soul Reaving
perks.description: Collect Soul Globes from dead enemies to restore 50 health.

perks.name: Shadow Blink
perks.description: Shadow Step's cast time and cooldown are 25% faster, but the range is reduced by 25%.

perks.name: Trigger Finger
perks.description: Refresh Dire Triggers' cooldown whenever using an ability or reloading.

changes.text: Pickup radius of Soul Globes increased from 5 to 8 meters.
Lifesteal increased from 25% to 30%.

comments: Reaper's reduced health pool has limited his ability to sustain through extended engagements. Increasing the effectiveness of his passive restores some of that durability while rewarding aggressive play.

changes.text: Health reduced from 300 to 275.
Movement speed bonus reduced from 40% to 30%.

comments: Dire Triggers has increased Reaper’s strengths across many matchups and added more lethality to his kit. Combined with his survivability, this pushes him past intended durability and kill potential. Reducing his health lowers his survivability while preserving the lethality Dire Triggers provides.

changes.text: Moved from Perk to Baseline ability.
Cooldown increased from 3 to 6 seconds.
Added.
Using an ability or reloading refreshes Dire Triggers’ cooldown.

comments: Dire Triggers has been moved into Reaper’s base kit to give him more consistent mid‑range options on a cooldown. This change adds additional decision‑making and skill expression to his gameplay.

changes.text: No longer cleanses on use.
Lifesteal reduced from 30% to 25%.

comments: Reaper’s sustain from his passive leads to high survivability in close-range duels. A slight reduction in lifesteal maintains his durability while reducing his self-healing reliability in extended engagements.

changes.text: Movement speed while active reduced from 50% to 40%
Moved from Minor to Major Perk
Removed
New Minor Perk
Leaving Wraith Form grants 40% movement speed for 2 seconds.
Removed.
New Minor Perk.
Shadow Step's cast time and cooldown are 25% faster, but the range is reduced by 25%.
Ultimate cost increased 9%.
Damage per pellet increased from 5.4 to 5.75 (108 to 115 per volley).

comments: Developer Comments: Part of the reason heroes like Reaper and Tracer had their damage reduced in the past was due to the shift to the 5v5 format—solo tanking and less frequent peeling made flanking heroes more effective—along with their strong performance on certain maps and game modes like Push and Flashpoint. This is now less of a concern with the introduction of map voting and hero bans, which help limit overperformance, so we're restoring some of their damage potency.

changes.text: Recovery reduced from 0.7 to 0.5 seconds.

comments: Developer comments: We're aligning the recovery of Dire Triggers with Reaper’s primary fire to improve the flow when alternating between the two.

changes.text: Recovery time reduced from 0.9 to 0.7 seconds.

comments: Developer Comments: The recovery time change will allow Reaper to weave primary fire shots between uses of Dire Trigger, reducing the friction of using this ability.

changes.text: Shadow Step reloads Hellfire Shotguns and has 25% increased range.
Collect Soul Globes from dead enemies to restore 50 health.
Use Secondary Fire to fire a volley with long range accuracy from both Hellfire Shotguns.
Leaving Wraith Form grants 40% additional lifesteal for 3 seconds.
Hitscan radius small reduced from 0.05 to 0.04 meters.
Lifesteal reduced from 35 to 30%.

comments: Developer Comments The added survivability from this passive is being tuned down now that Reaper has 300 health and more reliable mobility after the cast time reduction to Shadow Step.

changes.text: Weapon spread reduced from 6.5 to 6 degrees.
Cast time reduced from 1.5 to 1.2 seconds.

comments: Developer Comments: With the previous patch change to how armor reduces damage, shotgun weapon heroes like Reaper lost some value since much of their gameplan revolved around pressuring large tank heroes. To help shift Reaper toward being more effective against smaller targets we're tightening the weapon spread on the Hellfire Shotguns and reducing the amount of time enemies have to react to his Shadow Step teleport.

changes.text: Damage per second increased from 170 to 185.
Ultimate cost decreased by 12%.
+0.05 meters for hitscan projectiles with a high rate of fire or spread (e.g., Tracer's Pulse Pistols or Reaper's Hellfire Shotguns).
+0.08 meters for hitscan projectiles that are more precise (e.g., Cassidy's Peacekeeper or Soldier:76's Heavy Pulse Rifle).
+0.05 meters for travel time projectiles that are shotguns or have a very high rate of fire (e.g., Roadhog's Scrap Gun or Ramattra's Void Accelerator).
+0.10 meters for travel time projectile with a speed greater than 50 meters per second (e.g., Zenyatta's Destruction Orb).
+0.15 meters for travel time projectile with a speed less than or equal to 50 meters per second (e.g., Pharah's Rocket Launcher).
Very large projectiles with a base size greater than 0.5 meters have been excluded from these increases (e.g., Orisa's Energy Javelin or Reinhardt's Fire Strike).
150-175 HP heroes increased by 25 HP.
200-300 HP heroes increased by 50 HP.
300+ HP (Tanks) increased by 75-100 HP.
Each hero's precise health increases are listed in their patch notes below.
All Ultimate ability costs increased by 10%.
All heroes now regenerate 20 health per second after 5 seconds of not taking damage.
Reload speed bonus on elimination has been removed.
New role passive: Dealing damage reduces enemy healing received by 20% for 2 seconds.
Damage increased from 30 to 40.
Health increased from 250 to 300.
Can no longer be activated while affected by mobility-locking effects (Magnetic Grenade, Steel Trap, Graviton Surge, etc.).

comments: Developer Comment: The Reaper and Moira changes are addressing an inconsistency with the interaction of Wraith Form or Fade with mobility-locking effects such as Junkrat's Steel Trap, Sigma's Gravitic Flux, Zarya's Graviton Surge, and Cassidy's Magnetic Grenade. They are now disabled similarly to Tracer's Recall or Sombra's Translocator, which are abilities that also phase out and can move the player.

changes.text: Ultimate cost reduced 8%
Spread reduced from 8 to 7 degrees
Phase effects no longer clear the Zarya Graviton Surge or Sigma Gravitic Flux movement restriction effects
E.g., Reaper can still use Wraith Form while in Graviton Surge to prevent damage but can’t walk out of it
Sombra Hack effect is now removed by phase effects

Can now be used in air
Time to exit Shadow Step reduced from 1.0 second to 0.5 of a second
Reaper is now invisible for the entire time it takes to exit shadow step
Railings and other breakable objects no longer block teleporting
Disabled by Zarya’s Graviton Surge and Junkrat’s Steel Trap
